analysis:
The only change in this batch is to docs/developer/build.md, which is documentation. No patch hunks were supplied, so I compared the base excerpt (lines 933-1258) with the head excerpt (lines 1-443) as given. I saw no code, configuration or workflow changes that touch a threat-model asset or trust boundary.

Security-relevant statements in the head text that later passes should check against the actual code and workflows:
- Head lines 257-263 describe official-build registration. `provider-release-publication.py` registers the exact signed build through the scoped `POST /v1/releases`, and the platform persistence change must deploy first. No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required. Secret-bearing release jobs accept only verified signed annotated tags in reviewed `master` ancestry, or trusted `master` for dev/manual/recovery runs. They use repository-scoped secrets 'without environment approval attachments'. Related threat IDs are A-005, A-011, A-017 and T-054, plus TB-006 and TB-011.
- Head lines 334-336 say protected signing and publication jobs 'retain their existing approvals'. That wording sits uneasily with the 'without environment approval attachments' wording at lines 259-263. I could not tell whether either line is new in this PR. The release supply chain is out of scope in the threat model.
- Head lines 20-26 describe the native qualification entry as compiled into the ordinary CLI but refusing without explicit opt-in and a verified release app. The gate itself lives in code that was not supplied, so I could not check it.
- Lines 11 and 16-18 on provider tests and daemon-state isolation are benign.

I raised no findings because the changes are documentation only and consistent with the canonical threat-model context. The code and workflow claims above are unchecked, since the underlying files were not in this batch.
